The news: Quantum computing software company Q-CTRL has raised USD290 million ($415 million) at a valuation above USD1 billion in a series C round led by Salesforce Ventures.
The context: Q-CTRL’s products help make quantum computing useful by correcting errors and improving performance. It also builds Ironstone Opal, a quantum positioning system that enables geolocation without the need for GPS. Customers include Lockheed Martin, Airbus and IBM.
The round required two expansions to meet the level of investor demand. Among the new investors is the federal government’s National Reconstruction Fund, which has tipped in $70 million.
Other new investors include Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners and SPARX Asset Management.
Returning investors include Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures and Square Peg.
What they said: “The investor syndicate we’ve assembled showcases the strength of our technology, revenue growth, and strategic alignment with some of the most important sectors today, from AI to aviation,” Q-CTRL CEO and founder Michael Biercuk said.
Salesforce Ventures partner Robert Keith said: “The hard problem in quantum is not building the machine, it is getting useful output from it. Q-CTRL solves that with AI-powered control software, and the proof is already public: a materials simulation on IBM hardware that any developer can now call directly from the IBM Quantum Platform, and the first quantum navigation system qualified for safety of flight.”
“That software layer will decide whether quantum shows up in enterprise data centers this decade, and it is why Salesforce Ventures led this round,” Keith said.
The sources: Q-CTRL media release , NRF media release

Published

By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent

Key Points Science's $400 million Series D funds European expansion of PRIMA while US approval…
View more
Science's $400 million Series D funds European expansion of PRIMA while US approval remains pending.
PRIMA is CE marked in the EU but still requires FDA Humanitarian Device Exemption review before US sale.
The biohybrid neural-interface program remains research-stage with therapeutic uses still undefined.
Science Corporation announced on November 17, 2026 that it raised a $400 million Series D to expand availability of its PRIMA retinal implant in Europe, prepare for a US launch, and increase investment in its biohybrid neural-interface program.
Khosla Ventures, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Tenet Healthcare, 885 Capital, Y Combinator and PLC Neurotech participated, among other investors. The round brings total capital raised since Science’s founding in 2021 to more than $900 million. The company will also expand its research, manufacturing and operational infrastructure.
PRIMA’s Commercial and Regulatory Path
PRIMA is a retinal implant being studied for geographic atrophy caused by dry age-related macular degeneration. Science describes it as the first brain-computer interface CE marked in the European Union to restore form vision—the ability to read letters, numbers and words—for patients blinded by certain types of late-stage macular degeneration. It is registered for supply in the United Kingdom and is not approved or available for sale in any other country.
The implant contains 378 light-powered pixels that convert light from the system’s glasses into signals that stimulate retinal cells. The glasses combine a front-facing camera with an eye-facing projector that shines light precisely onto the implant. The design is intended to replicate the function of light-sensitive cells that have been lost.
At 12 months, 80% of patients in the PRIMA clinical study showed clinically meaningful improvement in visual acuity, and 84% reported reading letters, numbers and words at home with the system, according to Science’s product page. The reported efficacy results include the use of digital zoom and contrast.
In a July 22, 2026 announcement , Science said PRIMA had received two FDA Humanitarian Use Device designations. The program provides expedited review for devices treating rare diseases or conditions, but designation is not marketing approval: PRIMA must still be reviewed and approved through a Humanitarian Device Exemption. One designation covers blindness in both eyes caused by an advanced subset of geographic atrophy, without vision loss from other eye diseases; the other covers vision loss from Stargardt disease, a rare inherited retinal disease. The US approval process remains underway.
Biohybrid Neural-Interface Research
Science’s biohybrid architecture takes a different approach from the retinal implant: it anchors hundreds of thousands of engineered neurons to a device and uses their projections to form connections with neurons in the brain. MicroLEDs stimulate the embedded neurons, which are modified through optogenetics so they can be activated by light, while electrodes record their activity. articles.snippet:
Zilch has increased its securitization and corporate debt facilities by £165 million, bringing total commitments to £395 million as the payments company expands its product offering. Deutsche Bank led the latest financing, with participation from two major credit funds. The facilities will enable Zilch to originate up to £6 billion in lending annually.
The post Zilch: £395 Million Debt Facilities Expand Consumer Lending Capacity appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Zilch: £395 Million Debt Facilities Expand Consumer Lending Capacity
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:33 PM
Zilch: £395 Million Debt Facilities Expand Consumer Lending Capacity
Zilch has increased its securitization and corporate debt facilities by £165 million, bringing total commitments to £395 million as the payments company expands its product offering. Deutsche Bank led the latest financing, with participation from two major credit funds. The facilities will enable Zilch to originate up to £6 billion in lending annually.
The additional capacity supports customer growth and demand for products including Pay Monthly, launched in August 2026. That offering allows qualifying customers to spread purchases over three, six or 12 months.
Zilch is targeting a broader range of spending needs, including larger purchases such as holidays, household appliances and insurance premiums.
Average annual spending per active customer has reached £2,500, while the company’s gross merchandise value run rate has exceeded £3.5 billion.
The financing follows Zilch’s announcement that it surpassed a $300 million annual run rate and recorded two consecutive quarters of adjusted profit before tax in its 2027 financial year.
The company also plans to move into a new London headquarters in spring 2027, more than doubling its office capacity.
Founded in 2018, Zilch combines debit, credit, installments, earned wage access, credit-building features, offers and rewards within its payments platform.
The expanded funding facilities provide more lending capacity as that product mix develops. Management identified access to efficient funding as important to supporting higher transaction volumes and continued growth.
Chief Financial Officer Hugh Courtney said the financing reflects funders’ confidence in Zilch’s underwriting and ability to scale profitably in the United Kingdom.
The company’s strategy is to serve more customer payment needs through the same platform, strengthening engagement as users move between everyday spending and larger purchases.
KEY QUOTES:
“As we continue to grow at significant scale, having access to efficient funding is a key parameter for success. These expanded facilities give us greater capacity to support our customers where they need us, capturing more of the transactions that matter to customers day to day and providing the most rewarding ways to pay. By serving a broader range of customer needs, we can continue building a highly engaged customer relationship and delivering the value, flexibility and features that our customers really want.”
Philip Belamant, CEO And Co-Founder Of Zilch
“We are proud of our close partnerships with our funders, led by Deutsche Bank, who continue to support our growth as we scale the business profitably in the UK. The upsizing of the facilities represents a strong endorsement of our underwriting capabilities, product market fit and ability to continue scaling at pace.”
Hugh Courtney, Chief Financial Officer Of Zilch

articles.text:
LPL Financial Brings In $390 Million Firm Contour Wealth Management
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:36 PM
LPL Financial Brings In $390 Million Firm Contour Wealth Management
LPL Financial has added Contour Wealth Management, a Pennsylvania-based financial advisory practice serving approximately $390 million in client assets, to its broker-dealer and registered investment advisory platforms. Financial advisor Joe Borgese, a certified financial planner, joins LPL from Cetera alongside a team focused on comprehensive financial planning and multigenerational client relationships.
Contour Wealth Management is based in Boyertown, Pennsylvania, outside Philadelphia.
The firm serves individuals and families, including educators, healthcare professionals, business owners, and clients across multiple generations.
Its planning approach emphasizes developing long-term relationships and adapting financial strategies as clients’ needs evolve.
Borgese began his career in financial services in 1990, initially working in banking before moving into other areas of the industry.
Over more than three decades, he has developed a practice centered on investment planning, retirement strategies, and broader financial guidance.
Contour Wealth Management works with some families across three generations, helping clients address financial needs ranging from retirement planning to college savings.
The practice begins each client engagement by establishing an understanding of the client’s goals, expectations, and personal circumstances.
Advisors then develop financial plans intended to adapt to changes involving careers, families, retirement, and other life events.
The firm’s services include financial planning, investment planning, and tax preparation, supported by working relationships with outside professionals.
The practice is supported by an experienced team that coordinates client relationships and ongoing financial planning needs.
Lindsey Borgese, also a certified financial planner, helps manage the office.
The team includes Diana C. Dugan, an enrolled agent, alongside Brian Christman, Cheryl Dietz, and Karen Walla.
Their responsibilities support client service, administration, and coordination across the firm’s financial planning activities.
Reasons For Joining LPL Financial
Contour Wealth Management selected LPL Financial based on its technology infrastructure, operational support, and advisor-focused service model.
The practice also identified potential cost efficiencies for clients as an important consideration.
LPL provides brokerage, advisory, technology, and practice management services to independent financial advisors and financial institutions.
Its infrastructure is designed to allow advisors to operate their businesses while accessing a broader range of investment products and operational resources.
For Contour Wealth Management, the transition provides access to additional technology and support capabilities while preserving its relationship-driven planning approach.
Borgese believes these resources will help the practice operate more efficiently and continue delivering personalized financial guidance.
The move also reflects the broader appeal of independent advisory platforms that allow practices to maintain their identity while benefiting from the resources of larger financial services organizations.

articles.title: Exus Closes $345 Million Financing Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives
articles.snippet: Exus Closes $345 Million Financing Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives Hoodline
articles.text:
Source: Nikki / Wikimedia Commons
Exus Renewables North America said Thursday it closed $345 million in senior secured holding company financing led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, money the company says will go toward construction and new U.S. wind, solar and battery projects.
The check is another in a run of company financings and project deals, not a map of which turbines or panels get the cash. Exus framed the close against rising U.S. electricity demand and described itself as an independent owner, developer and operator of utility-scale renewable energy and storage.
What the Money Is For
Exus said the financing will support construction costs and development across its growing U.S. portfolio of wind, solar and battery storage assets. The announcement does not name the projects that will draw on the facility or split the dollars among those three technologies.
President and CEO Jim Spencer said the financing lets the company keep its momentum going. He also said Goldman Sachs Alternatives' support reflects confidence in Exus and gives it flexibility to build projects and bring generation online, including work already underway and a deeper pipeline.
Vikas Agrawal, managing director and co-head of Energy Transition Climate Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, said Exus has a strong platform for developing and operating utility-scale renewable projects. "We're pleased to support its continued investment in new energy infrastructure," he said, tying that support to growing U.S. electricity demand.
A Larger Company-Reported Book
Exus reported more than 800 megawatts operating or under construction and a total portfolio exceeding 6 gigawatts. Those are company figures, not an outside audit of nameplate capacity.
The comparison that is on the record is Exus' own July 22, 2025 financing announcement. Then, the company reported more than 5 gigawatts in its total portfolio and 764 megawatts operating or under construction, alongside $308.2 million in financing for the 185-megawatt Zia Solar portfolio in New Mexico and the 169-megawatt Keystone wind portfolio in Pennsylvania.
From that July 2025 snapshot to Thursday's release, the company-reported operating-or-under-construction figure moved from 764 megawatts to more than 800, and the total portfolio from over 5 gigawatts to more than 6. Exus also said it is expanding its operational footprint to meet growing national energy needs, with work that includes developing, repowering and managing renewable assets.
Separate Deals, Not One Stack
This holding-company financing sits beside other Exus transactions that the available reporting treats as separate. pv magazine USA reported in January that Exus had closed a $400 million senior secured corporate credit facility tied to a 4.5-gigawatt pipeline. Nothing in the Thursday announcement establishes whether that facility is still outstanding or how it relates to the $345 million.
Project-level money has also moved on its own track. On Sept. 22, Exus said it had completed the Highland North and Cambria wind repower projects in Cambria County, Pennsylvania, and that construction was financed through roughly $356 million led by KeyBanc Capital Markets. A week later, on Sept. 29, Exus and ibV Energy Partners announced that Exus had acquired four solar projects totaling 715 megawatts-peak.

articles.text:
Renewables
Exus Renewables North America Closes $345 Million in Financing to Support New Projects
Press Release
Monday, November 16, 2026
SHARE:
Exus Renewables North America, an independent owner, developer, and operator of utility-scale renewable energy and energy storage projects, has announced the closing of $345 million in senior secured holding company financing led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives. The financing will support construction costs and the development of new projects across Exus’ growing U.S. portfolio of wind, solar and battery storage assets.
The financing announced November 12 builds on an active year for Exus , including the closing of a $400 million senior secured corporate credit facility in December and approximately $356 million in project-level construction financing for its Highland North and Cambria wind projects in Pennsylvania in July . With more than 800 MW operating or under construction and a total portfolio exceeding 6 GW, Exus continues to advance its project pipeline amid rising U.S. electricity demand.
“We have projects moving forward and a deep pipeline behind them, and this financing lets us keep that momentum going,” said Jim Spencer, president and CEO of Exus Renewables North America. “The support from Goldman Sachs Alternatives reflects confidence in our team and our projects, and gives us the flexibility to keep building and bring new generation online where it’s needed.”
“Exus has established a strong platform for developing and operating utility-scale renewable energy projects,” said Vikas Agrawal, managing director and co-head of Energy Transition Climate Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. “We’re pleased to support its continued investment in new energy infrastructure as electricity demand grows across the United States.”
PEI Global Partners served as financial advisor to Exus on the transaction. Latham & Watkins LLP served as legal counsel to Exus, while Vinson & Elkins LLP served as legal counsel to Goldman Sachs Alternatives.

articles.title: Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing
articles.snippet: Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing Ohio Tech News
articles.text:
Startups + VC
Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing
Annual recurring revenue grew 17-fold over 18 months as the Columbus startup added industrial deployments. Customers include HII, Lockheed Martin and Saronic, while a $600 million performance-based shipbuilding agreement and plans to reach 400 employees by year-end underscore its growth.
Ohio Tech News
10 Nov 2026
— 3 min read
Share
Path Robotics co-founders and brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (Photo: Path Robotics)
Columbus-based Path Robotics has raised $300 million in Series E financing at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation to expand its robotic welding business and bring its artificial intelligence technology to more manufacturing tasks.
AI-focused growth equity firm Georgian led the round, announced Nov. 10, with participation from existing investors including Drive Capital. The financing brings Path’s total funding to more than $610 million since its founding in 2018, according to the company. Georgian partner Emily Walsh will join its board of directors.
The investment follows rapid commercial growth. Path said annual recurring revenue increased 17-fold over the past 18 months as it expanded deployments among industrial customers across North America.
The new capital will support additional deployments, development of new robotic platforms, and increased investment in computing resources and AI model training. In a LinkedIn post , CEO and co-founder Andy Lonsberry said Path plans to begin expanding its technology beyond welding into other production-line tasks in 2027.
“Our goal isn't to automate one step, but to automate the entire factory,” Lonsberry said in the announcement.
Scaling across shipbuilding and heavy industry
Path’s expansion targets a production challenge: manufacturers with demand for more products but limited capacity to build them.
The company develops physical AI—technology that enables robots to perceive their surroundings and adapt their actions to changing conditions. Its initial focus has been welding, where variations in parts and joints can make conventional, preprogrammed automation difficult to deploy.
Path said its customers include HII, Lockheed Martin and Saronic, along with manufacturers such as EK Machine, Millerbernd Manufacturing Company, TransAmerican Power Products and TYCROP. Its target industries include shipbuilding and defense, heavy equipment, and energy infrastructure.
Earlier this year, Path announced a $600 million performance-based production agreement with HII to accelerate deployment of its technology across U.S. Navy shipbuilding programs. That agreement is separate from the equity financing announced Nov. 10.
To support growing demand, Path said its workforce has increased 97% year over year, with plans to reach 400 employees by the end of 2026.
Taking its AI beyond welding
At the center of Path’s technology is Obsidian, a physical AI welding model that uses real-world production data to help robots identify weld joints, plan and execute welds, and adapt to changing conditions, according to the company.
Path recently introduced Rove, a mobile welding system that pairs Obsidian with a four-legged robot. The system is designed to bring welding capabilities directly to a part rather than requiring the work to take place inside a stationary robotic cell.
The funding will help Path extend its technology to additional robotic platforms and manufacturing applications.

articles.title: Welding AI Maker Path Robotics Raises $300M Series E With NAVER Ventures
articles.snippet: Welding AI Maker Path Robotics Raises $300M Series E With NAVER Ventures Wowtale
articles.text:
Skilled welders are hard to find, and shipyards and heavy-equipment plants are sitting on full order books. Traditional industrial robots do not help much here. They follow pre-programmed paths, which makes them a poor fit for welds that differ slightly from one part to the next. Path Robotics , a Columbus, Ohio-based startup, is betting that a robot that can see and decide for itself can fill that gap. On Nov. 10, the company announced a $300 million Series E at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation.
Georgian , an AI-focused growth equity firm, led the round. NAVER Ventures and D. E. Shaw Ventures joined as new investors, and existing backers Addition, Drive Capital, IronArc Ventures, Tiger Global, and Yamaha Motor Ventures also took part. Georgian partner Emily Walsh will join Path’s board.
Giving the robot eyes and judgment
A conventional welding robot has to be taught its path step by step, and a part that sits slightly out of place can ruin the weld. Path’s physical AI welding model, Obsidian, takes that teaching out of the loop. The robot finds the weld joint on its own, plans the sequence and path, welds, and adjusts when conditions change mid-job. The model learns from real-world welding data. For a factory, that means variable welds without reprogramming the robot each time.
The company recently added Rove, a mobile welding system that puts Obsidian on a quadruped robot. Instead of bringing the part to a welding cell, the robot walks to the part. Path says it shows the same model can run on different robot bodies.
ARR up 17x in 18 months, led by shipbuilding and defense
Path says its annual recurring revenue grew 17-fold over the past 18 months, though it did not disclose a dollar figure. The growth has come from shipbuilding and defense, heavy equipment, and energy infrastructure. Customers include HII, the largest U.S. shipbuilder, Lockheed Martin, and the maritime defense company Saronic , along with mid-sized manufacturers such as EK Machine, Millerbernd Manufacturing, TransAmerican Power Products, and TYCROP. Earlier this year, Path announced a $600 million performance-based production agreement with HII to deploy physical AI across U.S. Navy shipbuilding programs. Headcount has grown 97% over the past year, and the company plans to reach 400 employees by year-end.
CEO and co-founder Andy Lonsberry said Path started with welding because it is one of the hardest jobs on the factory floor to automate. “Our goal isn’t to automate one step, but to automate the entire factory,” he said. Founded in 2018, Path has now raised more than $610 million. The new money will go toward scaling the welding business, expanding to tasks before and after welding and to new robot form factors, and training AI models.
Georgian pointed to Path’s proprietary models and its growing base of production data, which it said improves the system with every deployment. Lockheed Martin Ventures called the investment an important milestone for strengthening the U.S. defense industrial base.
Competition: welding specialists and general-purpose robot AI
A handful of newer companies are going after the same problem. Korea’s RB-Ware makes a no-code welding robot and has installed more than 250 units in 16 countries, and NeoArcRobotics is building cutting and welding robots for Korean shipyards. articles.title: Path Robotics: $300 Million Series E At $2.45 Billion Valuation Funds Manufacturing AI Expansion
articles.snippet:
Path Robotics has raised $300 million in Series E financing at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation, providing capital to expand its physical AI technology beyond welding into additional manufacturing tasks and robotic platforms. Georgian led the round, with participation from existing investors Addition, Drive Capital, IronArc Ventures, Tiger Global, Yamaha Motor Ventures and its affiliates. D. E. Shaw Ventures and NAVER Ventures also participated. Georgian Partner Emily Walsh will join Path Robotics’ board of directors.
